findings.title: Interaction-mode radio buttons lack keyboard radio behavior
findings.trigger: Keyboard user focuses an Automatic or Manual option and presses an arrow key or tabs through the radio group.
findings.actual: The group and buttons expose radio roles and aria-checked, but both buttons stay tabbable and no arrow-key or roving-tabindex behavior exists.
findings.expected: One selected radio is tabbable; arrow keys move selection and focus within the group and the selected state remains announced.
findings.smallestFix: Add roving tabIndex and a shared arrow-key handler that changes and focuses the target option.

findings.title: Expanded MCP guide video lacks focus containment and restoration
findings.trigger: User expands the guide video, tabs through the dialog, or closes it with Escape.
findings.actual: The portal declares an aria-modal dialog and autofocuses Close, but does not trap focus or restore focus to the expand control after close.
findings.expected: Focus stays in the modal while open and returns to the invoking control after Escape or Close.
findings.smallestFix: Store the expand-button ref, add a small focus trap or existing dialog primitive, and restore focus after closing.

findings.title: Activity export has no pending state or duplicate-action guard
findings.trigger: User activates Export safe log repeatedly before api.exportLogs() settles or while export is slow.
findings.actual: Every activation starts another export; the button has no disabled or busy state and no local completion status.
findings.expected: Only one export runs at a time and the control announces loading, completion, or failure.
findings.smallestFix: Add local exporting state, disable the button around the promise, and expose a short status message while retaining the error toast.

findings.title: MCP stepper does not expose current or completed state semantically
findings.trigger: Screen-reader user navigates the MCP wizard after changing steps or after verification completes.
findings.actual: Active/completed state is conveyed by CSS classes and icon replacement; buttons have no aria-current step and no announced completion state.
findings.expected: Assistive technology receives the current and completed states conveyed visually while earlier-step navigation remains available.
findings.smallestFix: Add aria-current=step to the active button and a localized completion phrase to completed accessible names or descriptions.
